summary.plain: KEK's Tsukuba campus, Japan's oldest national particle-physics laboratory: the three-kilometre KEKB/SuperKEKB collider ring that has driven the Belle and Belle II experiments since 1998, and the site of the historic 12 GeV proton synchrotron that drove the world's first long-baseline accelerator neutrino beam, K2K.
